step.message: Which controls do we need for an internal chatbot that answers HR policy questions?

out.message:
Recommended baseline controls for this use case, in priority order:
1. Register the system in the AI inventory with a named accountable business owner and technical owner, and capture owner acceptance. (EI-03, EI-01)
2. Run the use case through intake triage and record a human-confirmed risk tier with rationale in the intake register. (EI-02)
3. Version system prompts and templates in a registry linked to model versions and change tickets. (EI-05)
4. Document every data source, its classification and the data flows into prompts, retrieval indexes, logs and external services. (EI-06)
5. Deploy redaction/masking on prompts, responses, logs and external model calls; test it against representative records and retain the results. (IS-04)
6. Restrict data access to the minimum records and fields required, using scoped service identities, and review access periodically. (IS-03, IS-11)
7. Run adversarial testing for direct and indirect prompt injection, jailbreaks and data leakage before release and after each material change. (IS-14)
8. Enforce a versioned runtime policy for input/output filtering, PII detection and topic restrictions, starting in monitor mode then enforce. (IS-12)
9. Complete a tier-proportionate risk and impact assessment and obtain approval at the tier-appropriate gate before (further) production use. (GL-02)

step.message: What controls apply to a customer support chatbot that reads CRM data?

out.message:
Recommended baseline controls for this use case, in priority order:
1. Register the system in the AI inventory with a named accountable business owner and technical owner, and capture owner acceptance. (EI-03, EI-01)
2. Register the agent and a tool/permission manifest listing each tool, scope and permitted action. (EI-07)
3. Deploy redaction/masking on prompts, responses, logs and external model calls; test it against representative records and retain the results. (IS-04)
4. Restrict data access to the minimum records and fields required, using scoped service identities, and review access periodically. (IS-03, IS-11)
5. Run adversarial testing for direct and indirect prompt injection, jailbreaks and data leakage before release and after each material change. (IS-14)
6. Add clear AI-interaction and AI-generated-content disclosures at the point of interaction; have Legal review the wording. (IS-08)
7. Enforce a versioned runtime policy for input/output filtering, PII detection and topic restrictions, starting in monitor mode then enforce. (IS-12)
8. Require human approval for high-impact actions via runtime policy, and record approver identity for each approval. (IS-13)
9. Log every tool call with trace ID, redacted inputs, decision and outcome to tamper-evident storage with defined retention. (SE-08)

## 9. Runtime guardrail recommendations

- **RG-PII-REDACTION** — Redact personal and sensitive data in prompts, responses and logs (IS-04, IS-03)
- **RG-INJECTION-FILTER** — Detect and block prompt-injection and jailbreak attempts, including indirect injection in retrieved content (IS-14, IS-12)
- **RG-TOOL-ALLOWLIST** — Allow-list tools and scopes per agent; deny by default (IS-11, EI-07)
- **RG-HUMAN-APPROVAL** — Require human approval for high-impact actions (refunds, record changes, external messages, deletions) (IS-13, IS-09)
- **RG-LIMITS** — Enforce rate, token, spend and per-action value limits (IS-16, IS-12)
- **RG-ACTION-LOGGING** — Log every model and tool call with trace ID, redacted inputs and policy decision (SE-08)
- **RG-KILL-SWITCH** — Provide a kill switch to disable the system, agent or individual tools (IS-15)
- **RG-DISCLOSURE** — Display AI-interaction disclosure to end users (IS-08)

## 9. Runtime guardrail recommendations

- **RG-PII-REDACTION** — Redact personal and sensitive data in prompts, responses and logs (IS-04, IS-03)
- **RG-INJECTION-FILTER** — Detect and block prompt-injection and jailbreak attempts, including indirect injection in retrieved content (IS-14, IS-12)
- **RG-TOOL-ALLOWLIST** — Allow-list tools and scopes per agent; deny by default (IS-11, EI-07)
- **RG-HUMAN-APPROVAL** — Require human approval for high-impact actions (refunds, record changes, external messages, deletions) (IS-13, IS-09)
- **RG-LIMITS** — Enforce rate, token, spend and per-action value limits (IS-16, IS-12)
- **RG-ACTION-LOGGING** — Log every model and tool call with trace ID, redacted inputs and policy decision (SE-08)
- **RG-KILL-SWITCH** — Provide a kill switch to disable the system, agent or individual tools (IS-15)
- **RG-DISCLOSURE** — Display AI-interaction disclosure to end users (IS-08)

## 9. Runtime guardrail recommendations

- **RG-PII-REDACTION** — Redact personal and sensitive data in prompts, responses and logs (IS-04, IS-03)
- **RG-INJECTION-FILTER** — Detect and block prompt-injection and jailbreak attempts, including indirect injection in retrieved content (IS-14, IS-12)
- **RG-TOOL-ALLOWLIST** — Allow-list tools and scopes per agent; deny by default (IS-11, EI-07)
- **RG-HUMAN-APPROVAL** — Require human approval for high-impact actions (refunds, record changes, external messages, deletions) (IS-13, IS-09)
- **RG-LIMITS** — Enforce rate, token, spend and per-action value limits (IS-16, IS-12)
- **RG-ACTION-LOGGING** — Log every model and tool call with trace ID, redacted inputs and policy decision (SE-08)
- **RG-KILL-SWITCH** — Provide a kill switch to disable the system, agent or individual tools (IS-15)
- **RG-DISCLOSURE** — Display AI-interaction disclosure to end users (IS-08)

## 9. Runtime guardrail recommendations

- **RG-PII-REDACTION** — Redact personal and sensitive data in prompts, responses and logs (IS-04, IS-03)
- **RG-INJECTION-FILTER** — Detect and block prompt-injection and jailbreak attempts, including indirect injection in retrieved content (IS-14, IS-12)
- **RG-TOOL-ALLOWLIST** — Allow-list tools and scopes per agent; deny by default (IS-11, EI-07)
- **RG-HUMAN-APPROVAL** — Require human approval for high-impact actions (refunds, record changes, external messages, deletions) (IS-13, IS-09)
- **RG-LIMITS** — Enforce rate, token, spend and per-action value limits (IS-16, IS-12)
- **RG-ACTION-LOGGING** — Log every model and tool call with trace ID, redacted inputs and policy decision (SE-08)
- **RG-KILL-SWITCH** — Provide a kill switch to disable the system, agent or individual tools (IS-15)
- **RG-DISCLOSURE** — Display AI-interaction disclosure to end users (IS-08)

# Executive Readiness Report — Example Regional Bank (synthetic)

> **SYNTHETIC DRESS REHEARSAL.** Fictional organization, generated answers. This report demonstrates the VERITRAIL Pilot A workflow and outputs; it is not evidence about any real organization.

**Prepared:** 2026-10-21 · **Scope:** VERITRAIL Governance Baseline (Pilot A profile) · **Prepared by:** VERITRAIL Agent-assisted workflow, synthetic analyst

## 1. Executive summary

- **28 AI systems** registered as draft inventory records (EI-01); preliminary tiers: High-risk 12, Limited 14, Minimal 2. Tiers are Inferred and were confirmed through the approval queue (EI-02, IS-13).
- **Enterprise maturity: 48.1 / 100 — Developing** (self-reported, User-asserted).
- **12 deep-dive assessments** covering every High-risk-tier system; **403 gaps** identified (Critical 40, High 254, Medium 90, Low 19).
- **2 runtime policies** drafted for agentic systems; both remain in draft/observe mode pending human approval to activate (IS-12, IS-13).
- Evidence position: Missing evidence: 262, User-asserted: 101, Critical gap: 40.

## 2. AI portfolio by risk tier

| Tier | Systems | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| High-risk | 12 | SME credit decisioning model, Retail credit scorecard, Card fraud detection, KYC document verification |
| Limited | 14 | AML transaction monitoring, Chargeback dispute assistant, Marketing propensity model, Internal code assistant |
| Minimal | 2 | Meeting summariser, Branch staffing forecast |

## 3. Maturity baseline by domain

| Domain | Score |
|---|---|
| Strategy & Accountability | 53.3 |
| AI Inventory & Visibility | 40.0 |
| Risk Management & Lifecycle | 46.7 |
| Data & Privacy | 53.3 |
| Security & Resilience | 46.7 |
| Fairness, Safety & Transparency | 46.7 |
| Human Oversight & Operations | 53.3 |
| Assurance, Evidence & Improvement | 46.7 |

## 4. Risk heat map — gaps by system and severity

| System | Tier | Critical | High | Medium | Low |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Retail credit scorecard | High-risk | 5 | 21 | 5 | 2 |
| KYC document verification | High-risk | 4 | 19 | 5 | 2 |
| Biometric face match (ID&V) | High-risk | 2 | 25 | 3 | 1 |
| Collections outreach agent | High-risk | 6 | 26 | 8 | 2 |
| CV screening assistant | High-risk | 4 | 23 | 9 | 2 |
| SME credit decisioning model | High-risk | 1 | 19 | 8 | 1 |
| Card fraud detection | High-risk | 2 | 24 | 7 | 3 |
| Customer support agent | High-risk | 6 | 25 | 10 | 1 |
| Mortgage valuation model | High-risk | 1 | 22 | 8 | 1 |
| Robo-advice portfolio tool | High-risk | 4 | 17 | 8 | 2 |
| Employee attrition model | High-risk | 3 | 17 | 7 | 1 |
| Cyber threat detection | High-risk | 2 | 16 | 12 | 1 |

## 5. Most frequent Critical/High control gaps

| Control | Occurrences |
|---|---|
| IS-03 Privacy assessment and data minimisation | 28 |
| EI-05 Model, prompt and component registry | 25 |
| SE-04 AI incident management and reporting | 19 |
| SE-02 Evidence repository and retention | 18 |
| IS-08 Transparency and AI disclosures | 14 |
| GL-11 Vendor AI due diligence and contract controls | 14 |
| AO-09 Third-party AI accountability | 14 |
| GL-04 Change management and reassessment triggers | 13 |
| IS-06 Safety and harm evaluation | 13 |
| IS-10 Secure model and prompt supply chain | 12 |

## 6. Remediation roadmap

- **First 30 days:** close Critical gaps (owners and due dates in the gap register), stand up the AI system of record as authoritative (EI-01, EI-03), enable redaction and kill switch for agentic systems (IS-04, IS-15).
- **Days 31–60:** High gaps; adversarial testing of LLM apps and agents (IS-14); change triggers for model/prompt/tool changes (GL-04); move runtime policies from observe to warn/protect (IS-12).
- **Days 61–90:** Medium gaps; control-testing programme and evidence repository (SE-01, SE-02); leadership KPI pack (SE-03); enforce mode for agents after approval (IS-13).

## 7. Runtime Shield recommendations

| Agent | Policy | Version | Status | Rollout mode | Risk rating | Activation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Customer support agent | pol-customer-support-agent | 0.1.0 | draft | observe | High | apr_000030 (pending) |
| Collections outreach agent | pol-collections-outreach-agent | 0.1.0 | draft | observe | Critical | apr_000031 (pending) |

## 8. Pilot success metrics (dry run)

| Metric | Target | Result | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| AI systems registered | ≥ 25 | 28 | Met (synthetic) |
| High-risk systems assessed | 100% | 12/12 (100%) | Met (synthetic) |
| Agent-assisted assessment completion | ≥ 70% | 100% (all responses captured via agent tools; scripted) | Met (synthetic — not a measure of user adoption) |
| Critical gaps documented with owners | Yes | 40 critical gaps, all with owner role + due date | Met (synthetic) |
| Runtime policies drafted | ≥ 2 | 2 | Met (synthetic) |
| Executive report accepted | Yes | Report generated | Requires real partner |
| Follow-on commercial discussion initiated | Yes | — | Requires real partner |

## 9. Governance checks exercised

- W2: registered 28 AI systems as draft records
- W2: 28 tier confirmations approved by approver; separation-of-duties check: PASS — self-approval refused (ApprovalError)
